title: Analysis of Tubular Membrane Networks in Cardiac Myocytes from Atria and Ventricles
protocol: Handle animals gently according to approved protocols.
Inject each mouse with heparin (500 IU/kg body weight s.c.) at least 20 min prior to heart extraction.
Anesthetize mice aged 12 weeks or older by isoflurane inhalation.
Confirm the absence of pain withdrawal reflexes in anesthetized mice.
Euthanize animals by cervical dislocation.
Extract the heart swiftly following expert protocols.
Preserve the tissue of the proximal ascending aorta using stump forceps and straight scissors.
Establish a continuous transversal cutting edge through the aortic vessel wall.
Transfer the excised heart immediately into ice-cold nominally Ca2+ free perfusion buffer.
Keep the great vessels clamped during transfer through air into buffer to avoid inadvertent air embolism until the heart is fully submerged.
Use BDM in the buffer and ice-cooled solutions to inhibit cardiac contraction.
Cannulate the aorta under panoramic stereovision of the heart with a smooth, surface polished 21 G cannula.
Ensure that there are no air bubbles in the cannula by connecting a proximal solution reservoir through a 2-way Luer valve.
Confirm under binocular magnification that the cannula is positioned correctly inside the aorta.
Position the cannula approximately 1 mm above the aortic valves and coronary artery branches.
Avoid any passage through or inadvertent perforation of the aortic valves with the cannula.
Tie the aorta gently to custom-made, circumferentially oriented anti-slip grooves near the end of the cannula using two silk sutures.
Connect the solution-filled cannula tied to the aorta and heart to a tightly fitting outflow connector of a customized and pre-calibrated perfusion system.
Perfuse the heart as soon as possible for 4 min using oxygenated perfusion buffer at 37 °C (target perfusion rate: 4 ml/min).
Switch the perfusion to collagenase-containing digestion buffer (600 U/ml collagenase type II) for 8-10 min at 37 °C.
Monitor tissue digestion by confirming similar changes including increasing opaqueness, softness, and flaccidity throughout the apparent heart surface.
Dissect cardiac chambers as needed following digestion.
Place the cannulated heart under a binocular microscope.
Visualize the posterior heart wall.
Dissect residual non-cardiac tissue e.g., lung and vessel parts to avoid cell contamination in the digestion buffer using micro scissors.
Follow a check list which particular chambers, regions, and/or cells of the collagenase digested heart should be harvested.
Use a relatively wide and flat dissection bath coated with a several mm thick layer of silicone plastic elastomer.
Fix the apex of the heart with a fine insect steel pin to the bottom elastomer layer.
Deflect the right atrial appendage.
Dissect the right atrium just above the atrioventricular valves.
Continue the dissection with the left atrium.
Discard the fibrous valve apparatus.
Dissect the left and right free ventricular walls.
Dissect the septum.
Dissect smaller tissue parts as needed.
Transfer ventricular tissue into 2.5 ml fresh digestion buffer.
Dissect the entire ventricular tissue or specific parts (e.g., LV, RV, free walls, and/or septum) into approximately 1 mm³ pieces in 2.5 ml digestion buffer using sharp scissors.
Gently dissociate VMs into cell suspension by slow trituration of the tissue pieces with a transfer pipette.
Avoid any air bubbling in the cell suspension during the trituration process.
Add 8 ml of stop buffer to the VM cell suspension.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 ml conical tube.
Allow remaining tissue pieces to settle at the bottom for approximately 15 seconds.
Harvest the VM suspension by transferring the supernatant volume to a new 15 ml tube.
If excessive tissue pieces are present, use a minimally 200 µm spaced nylon mesh to separate the tissue from the cell suspension.
Let the VM cell suspension settle to the bottom of a 15 ml conical tube by gravity for 8 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and gently resuspend the remaining VM pellet in 10 ml of perfusion buffer.
Repeat wash step as needed (optional: add additional wash steps to gradually increase Ca2+ concentration).
Resuspend the settled VM pellet in 10 ml perfusion buffer.
Distribute the cell suspension volume into 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes, containing approximately 50,000 VM cells per tube.
Transfer the digested/dissected atrial tissue into 1 ml of fresh digestion buffer for AM cell isolation.
Cut partially digested atrial tissue into approximately 1 mm3 pieces in 1 ml digestion buffer using micro scissors.
Gently dissociate AM cells out of the digested tissue pieces into cell suspension using trituration with a 1 ml plastic pipette with a cut tip.
Add 4 ml of stop buffer to arrest any remaining collagenase activity in cell suspension.
Transfer the AM cell suspension into a 15 ml conical tube.
Allow the remaining tissue pieces to settle at the bottom for approximately 15 sec.
Harvest the supernatant volume containing the free AM cells via solution transfer to a new 15 ml tube.
Centrifuge the AM cell suspension, e.g., 2 min at 20 x g at RT or let the cells settle down slowly by gravity for 20 min in a 15 ml conical tube.
Discard the supernatant and gently resuspend the AM pellet in 5 ml perfusion buffer.
Repeat the wash step to resuspend AM cells gently in 5 ml perfusion buffer.
Distribute the cell suspension volume in 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes, approximately 1,000 AM cells per tube.
Dilute 500 μl of the cell suspension with 1:1 vol/vol trypan blue solution (final concentration 0.02%).
Mix the cells and the trypan blue gently by very slow up/down pipetting.
Apply the trypan blue containing cell suspension to a Neubauer-type improved cytometer.
Count the intact myocytes using an inverted microscope.
Exclude any cells with apparent damage, membrane blebs, disrupted striations, contractures, and cells accumulating intracellular trypan blue.
Exclude spontaneously contracting cells.
Use only cardiac myocytes with regular striations which exclude trypan blue throughout the cell volume for analysis.
Judge the integrity of individual atrial and ventricular myocytes by transmitted light microscopy.
Save the bright field image as a Tif file for documentation and further analysis.
Visualize the fluorescent signals of TATS membranes as described in section 3.
Overlay the fluorescent images with cell-specific bright field image morphology using ImageJ.
Determine the sarcomere length from the bright field images.
Measure the distance between sequentially aligned sarcomere striations.
Divide the measured distance by the number of sarcomeres to obtain mean sarcomere length.
Repeat measurements at least two locations per cell.
Quantify the morphology and dimensions of individual atrial and ventricular myocytes.
Measure the cell length, width, and area from transmitted light microscopy images.
Calculate the length:width ratio for each cell.
Analyze 2D cell dimensions using ImageJ polygon selection tool.
Add selected areas to ROI manager for further analysis.
Document specific mouse strain, age, sex, heart size, and any interventions for cells with expected morphological changes.
Load the imaging chamber with a 42 mm glass coverslip.
Prepare 20 μl of laminin solution by diluting 20 μl of laminin stock in physiological perfusion buffer (1:10).
Spread 20 μl of laminin solution evenly on the glass coverslip.
Dilute 20 μl of 2 mM di-8-ANEPPS stock solution in 780 μl physiological buffer to prepare a 50 µM di-8-ANEPPS solution.
Let the cells settle by gravity for 8 min in a 1.5 ml reaction tube.
Carefully remove the supernatant while avoiding unnecessary agitation of the cell pellet and gently resuspend the cell pellet in 800 μl of di-8-ANEPPS containing solution (50 µM).
Immediately transfer the di-8-ANEPPS/myocyte suspension onto the laminin-coated coverslip in the imaging chamber.
Stain the VM suspension for 15 min at RT in the dark.
Slowly remove excess volume via the upward fluid meniscus at the sides of the imaging chamber with a manual pipette.
Wash the attached myocyte suspension once by slowly adding 1 ml of perfusion buffer followed by removing any excess fluid including non-adherent cells.
Overlay the stained and surface attached myocytes with 1 ml of perfusion buffer slowly from the side of the imaging chamber.
Place the imaging chamber on the microscope stage.
Choose the best possible fluorescent microscope option(s) available for TATS membrane imaging.
Consider recent generation, modern fluorescence microscopes with optimized PMT array detectors and photon recycling pathways that maximize fluorescent signal intensity for confocal imaging.
Use a 63X 1.4 NA oil objective or – depending on availability – use a STED superresolution microscope for smallest TATS details as reviewed for myocyte-specific applications by Kohl et al.
Set imaging parameters for confocal laser scanning microscopy.
Use excitation at 458 nm, set to 3% maximal laser power.
Detect emitted signal between 550 nm and 740 nm.
Set detector gain (master command 800).
Adjust pinhole to 1 AU for an optical slice thickness of 900 nm.
Optimize imaging parameters for optimal signal-to-noise ratio.
Use bright field mode to select intact AM or VM cells.
Select cells based on criteria: regular striations, equal sarcomere spacing, sharp surface edges and serrations, continuous lateral membrane integrity, absence of blebs.
Take a sample image of a central intracellular myocyte section.
Adjust the ROI using the “crop” function.
Set crop window to adjust for cell dimensions.
Final pixel size measures 100 nm x 100 nm.
Adjust x-axis of the crop window to correspond with the major axis of the myocyte.
Select the final imaging plane manually using single image frames.
Confirm that T-tubule and A-tubule components of the TATS membranes are visually apparent in the focal plane.
Adjust the pixel dwell time to approximately 0.5 µsec.
Use 16x averaging and record the image as a snapshot.
Repeat the image snapshot step to establish the appropriate imaging plane for TATS membrane structures.
Save the final image in its target folder.
Confirm sufficient cell integrity off-line before analysis.
Exclude any damaged cells from analysis.
Open the image file of a di-8-ANEPPS stained myocyte in Fiji.
Save the image as a Tif file.
Select the appropriate region of interest excluding the outer surface membrane signal using the “polygon selection” tool.
Add the selected ROI to the “ROI Manager.”
Align the main longitudinal cell axis and the image x-axis in parallel for orientation analysis.
Clear any unwanted signal information from the outer surface membrane by editing "Clear Outside."
Ensure that the selected ROI only contains intracellular membrane portions corresponding to the TATS network.
Subtract background from the image.
Set the Rolling ball radius to 5 pixels.
Enhance local contrast using CLAHE.
Set the block size to 49, histogram bins to 256, maximum slope to 3, and mask to “none”.
Smooth the image.
Open Statistical Region Merging plugin.
Set parameters to Q100 and click on Show Averages.
Confirm complete processing indicated by a new image frame with the label “SRM Q=100” appearing.
Convert the image type to 8-bit.
Click on Image → Adjust → Threshold.
Choose a threshold sufficiently low to detect most TATS structures, starting with 40 as a baseline.
Document the final choice of threshold parameters.
Confirm correct superimposition of TATS image details versus extracted skeleton data.
Apply the identified threshold consistently across all images.
Repeat overlay comparison for original signal versus skeleton data.
Click on Apply: the image data becomes binary.
Click on Plugins → Skeleton → Skeletonize (2D/3D).
Save the skeletonized 2D image as a Tif file by clicking on File → Save as → Tif.
Analyze the skeletonized image file for quantitative data output using Plugins → Analyze Skeleton (2D/3D).
Choose Prune cycle method: none.
Confirm automatic generation of the resulting data table.
Save the automatically generated data table as a txt file.
Select relevant quantitative parameters such as the total number of branch points or the average branch length.
Use automated image processing routines including all necessary steps described under 4.5 to harmonize analysis between individual images and/or image batches.
Adjust the programming in the Supplementary Code File containing an image processing Macro programmed for Fiji as needed.
Analyze the individual orientations of all TATS network components from the skeletonized image data using the Fiji plugin “Directionality”.
Generate a directionality histogram where axially oriented A-tubule or transversally oriented T-tubule components are represented by 0° or 90° bins, respectively.
Ensure the x-axis of the image corresponds closely with the main (longitudinal) 0° axis of the VM cell.
Save the newly generated results table including associated histogram data as txt file.
Import skeletonized data parameters from all images into one combined Excel file.
Calculate and derive average values from the imported data in the Excel file.
Import directionality histogram data from the same grouped dataset into a combined Excel file.
Generate the average directionality histogram using the combined Excel file.
Analyze additional TATS network parameters of interest for individual or between different treatment groups as needed.
